explanation: Borges became director of Argentina's National Library in 1955, when he was almost blind. In a poem he marvelled that God had given him books and the night at once.

claims.text: Jorge Luis Borges wrote the story The Library of Babel, about a vast library that holds every possible book.
Julio Cortázar, Isabel Allende and Mario Vargas Llosa did not write The Library of Babel.
Borges became director of Argentina's National Library in 1955, by which time he was almost blind.
In his Poem of the Gifts, Borges wrote of God's irony in giving him 'books and the night' at the same time.
